Development

The Craft

Four stages, no shortcuts

A door takes six to ten weeks. We use athel wood, hand-forged iron, and pigments ground from ochre, indigo and charcoal bound in gum.

Survey

We document every surviving fragment of paint and carving, tracing patterns before any wood is touched.

Joinery

Planks are pegged, never glued, and the wooden lock — the mizlaj — is cut to fit its frame.

Carving

Triangles and rosettes are incised with chisels to give the paint a bed and the light a shadow.

Painting

Bands are laid freehand in natural pigment, then sealed with linseed to weather gracefully.

The story of the house

Built by hand, kept by family, for five generations.

In 1891, the Al-Rashed family raised these walls from mud, straw and palm trunks drawn from the wadi. The triangular openings let the hot air out; the thick walls kept the summer at bay.

SQLite at the edge, synced everywhere.

Driftdb runs an embedded SQL database beside every user and keeps every copy consistent through CRDTs. Reads are local and writes don't wait.

$npm install driftdb

Also available for Rust, Go, Python and Swift. No account needed.

How sync works, in one scroll

Each device holds a full replica. Changes move between replicas as small deltas, and conflicts resolve automatically with no locks and no round-trips.

01 · WRITE

Commit locally

Your app writes to the replica on the device or edge node. It returns in under a millisecond, even when offline.

02 · LOG

Record a delta

Every row change is stamped with a hybrid logical clock and appended to a compact change log.

03 · GOSSIP

Stream to peers

Deltas spread to the nearest regions over QUIC. Peers exchange only what the other side is missing.

04 · MERGE

Converge

CRDT merge rules guarantee that every replica reaches the same state, whatever order the deltas arrive in.
